questions.question_text: Select one correct statement regarding persistent delusional disorder:

options.text: Delusional disorder is associated with passivity phenomena
Delusions must be present for at least 3 months for a diagnosis
Depressive episodes invalidate the diagnosis
Persistent delusional disorder is associated with persistent hallucinations
Somatization is an important factor in persistent delusional disorder

correct_answer.text: Delusions must be present for at least 3 months for a diagnosis

correct_answers.text: Delusions must be present for at least 3 months for a diagnosis

questions.explanation: According to the ICD-10 classification, delusion constitutes the most conspicuous or the only clinical characteristic and must have been present for at least 3 months.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following eye signs is pathognomonic of multiple sclerosis?

options.text: Argyll Robertson pupil
Bilateral internuclear ophthalmoplegia
Holmes–Adie pupil
Horner's syndrome
Kayser–Fleischer ring

correct_answer.text: Bilateral internuclear ophthalmoplegia

correct_answers.text: Bilateral internuclear ophthalmoplegia

questions.explanation: A pathognomic feature of multiple sclerosis is bilateral internuclear ophthalmoplegia.

questions.question_text: Regarding apraxia, which of the following statements is false?

options.text: Motor system and sensorium should be sufficiently intact
Constructional apraxia can be tested by asking the patient to draw simple figures
Dressing apraxia is tested by asking the patient to put on some of his/her clothes
Ideomotor apraxia can be tested by increasingly complicated tasks to command
None of the above

correct_answer.text: None of the above

correct_answers.text: None of the above

questions.explanation: All are true.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is false?

options.text: Atopognosia is failure to identify letters written on skin
Astereognosis is failure to identify three-dimensional form
Finger agnosia is failure to identify which finger is touched
Anosognosia is failure to identify functional deficits caused by disease
Agnosia is inability to understand significance of sensory stimuli

correct_answer.text: Atopognosia is failure to identify letters written on skin

correct_answers.text: Atopognosia is failure to identify letters written on skin

questions.explanation: Atopognosia is failure to know the position of an object on the skin while agraphognosia is failure to identify letters or numbers written on the skin.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not an interviewer-rated scale?

options.text: Hamilton Rating Scale for Depression
Montgomery–A ˚sberg Depression Rating Scale
Yale–Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale
Beck Depression Inventory
Hamilton Anxiety Scale

correct_answer.text: Beck Depression Inventory

correct_answers.text: Beck Depression Inventory

questions.explanation: The Beck Depression Inventory is client rated.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true?

options.text: The Yale–Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale is a seven-point scale for obsessive compulsive disorder
The Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale has 10 items scored on a seven-point scale
The Hamilton Rating Scale for Depression measures symptoms of depression rather than the severity
The General Health Questionnaire has been primarily designed for diagnosis in primary care
The Hamilton Anxiety Scale should not be used to rate anxiety in patients with other disorders

correct_answer.text: The Hamilton Anxiety Scale should not be used to rate anxiety in patients with other disorders

correct_answers.text: The Hamilton Anxiety Scale should not be used to rate anxiety in patients with other disorders

questions.explanation: Yale–Brown is a four-point scale for 10 symptoms. The Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale has 16 items scored on seven-point scale. Hamilton measures severity rather than the symptoms. GHQ is a screening questionnaire used in primary care.

questions.question_text: Regarding reliability of an instrument, which of the following is false?

options.text: Interrater reliability measures degree of agreement between different raters
T est–retest reliability describes degree of correlation between two identical assessments at different times
Split-half reliability signifies the external consistency of a test
Intrarater reliability measures degree of agreement by the same rater at different times
The index of interrater reliability is kappa

correct_answer.text: Split-half reliability signifies the external consistency of a test

correct_answers.text: Split-half reliability signifies the external consistency of a test

questions.explanation: Split-half reliability signifies internal consistency.

questions.question_text: In relation to psychometric tests, which of the following is false?

options.text: Validity measures the degree to which a test can be replicated
Sensitivity is the degree to which a test measures true positives
A test with high specificity has a low type 1 error rate
A positive result in a high-specificity test rules in the disease
Negative predictive value is the proportion of patients with negative test results who are correctly diagnosed

correct_answer.text: Validity measures the degree to which a test can be replicated

correct_answers.text: Validity measures the degree to which a test can be replicated

questions.explanation: Validity measures the extent to which a test measures what it is designed to measure.

questions.question_text: In Alzheimer's dementia, all of the following symptoms can be seen, except:

options.text: Long-term memory loss
Depression
Disorders of language and praxis
Impairment of consciousness
Persecutory delusion

correct_answer.text: Impairment of consciousness

correct_answers.text: Impairment of consciousness

questions.explanation: Impairment of consciousness is seen in delirium rather than dementia.

questions.question_text: Gerstmann's syndrome includes:

options.text: Right-to-left disorientation
Acalculia
Dysgraphaesthesia
Finger agnosia
Dysgraphia

correct_answer.text: Dysgraphaesthesia

correct_answers.text: Dysgraphaesthesia

questions.explanation: Gerstmann's syndrome consists of all the other four symptoms.

questions.question_text: In Wernicke–Korsakoff's syndrome, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: Anterograde amnesia is a main feature of the syndrome
Hallucinations rule out Korsakoff's syndrome
Vision problems include double vision and drooping of the eyelid
Confabulation is very characteristic of the syndrome
It is caused by thiamine deficiency

correct_answer.text: Hallucinations rule out Korsakoff's syndrome

correct_answers.text: Hallucinations rule out Korsakoff's syndrome

questions.explanation: Korsakoff's psychosis consists of hallucinations and is a late stage of Wernicke's encephalopathy.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true regarding pseudohallucinations, except:

options.text: They are a form of imagery
They are experienced as located in external space but recognized as unreal
They are not diagnostic
They are experienced within the mind
They cannot be dismissed by an effort of will

correct_answer.text: They are a form of imagery

correct_answers.text: They are a form of imagery

questions.explanation: Pseudohallucinations resemble imagery but, unlike imagery, they cannot be dismissed by an effort of will.

questions.question_text: All of the following are false, except:

options.text: Eidetic imagery cannot be intense and detailed
Perception can be terminated by an effort of will
Pareidolia is a type of imagery
Imagery is the awareness of the percept that has arisen from the sense organs
A healthy person cannot distinguish between images and percepts

correct_answer.text: Pareidolia is a type of imagery

correct_answers.text: Pareidolia is a type of imagery

questions.explanation: Eidetic memory is visual imagery that is so intense and detailed that it has a 'photographic' quality. Perception can be attended to or ignored but cannot be terminated by an effort of will. Imagery is awareness of the percept that has arisen from the mind and not the sense organs. Images lack the sense of reality by which healthy people distinguish them from percepts.

questions.question_text: Regarding hallucinations, which of the following is false:

options.text: They can occur in healthy individuals
They cannot be terminated at will
They can occur after sensory deprivation
They are diagnostic of psychotic disorder
They can occur in seizures

correct_answer.text: They are diagnostic of psychotic disorder

correct_answers.text: They are diagnostic of psychotic disorder

questions.explanation: Hallucination is not diagnostic.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true regarding hallucinations:

options.text: Hallucinatory voices are sometimes called phonemes
Hallucinations of dwarf figures are called extracampine hallucinations
In second-person hallucination, voices refer to the patient as he or she
Elementary hallucination refers to experiences such as seeing faces and scenes
Gedankenlautwerden is when voices repeat the thoughts immediately after the patient has thought them

correct_answer.text: Hallucinatory voices are sometimes called phonemes

correct_answers.text: Hallucinatory voices are sometimes called phonemes

questions.explanation: Hallucinations of dwarf figures are called Lilliputian hallucinations. Voices refer to the patient as he or she in third-person hallucination, while in second-person hallucination voices talk to the patient. As the name explains, elementary hallucination refers to flashes of light, bangs, whistlers, etc. Gedankenlautwerden is voices that seem to speak the patient's thoughts as he /she is thinking them, while e ´cho de la pense ´ei s voices that seem to repeat the thoughts immediately after the patient has thought them.

questions.question_text: Select one correct statement from the following:

options.text: E´cho de la pense ´e is when voices seem to speak the patient's thoughts as he /she is thinking them
Olfactory and gustatory hallucinations are frequently experienced together
Hypnopompic hallucinations occur at the point of falling asleep
Haptic hallucination is a type of olfactory hallucination
Reflex hallucination is common in schizophrenia

correct_answer.text: Olfactory and gustatory hallucinations are frequently experienced together

correct_answers.text: Olfactory and gustatory hallucinations are frequently experienced together

questions.explanation: Hypnagogic hallucinations occur at point of sleep and hypnopompic at time of getting up. Haptic hallucinations are tactile hallucinations. Reflex hallucination is a rare condition.

questions.question_text: All of the following are types of loosening of association, except:

options.text: Verbigeration
Vorbeireden
Word salad
Knight's move
Over-inclusion

correct_answer.text: Over-inclusion

correct_answers.text: Over-inclusion

questions.explanation: Verbigeration is speech reduced to senseless repetition of sounds, words or phrases. Vorbeireden is talking past the point. Word salad is severe verbigeration. Knight's move is jumping from one topic to another. Over-inclusion is a disorder of thought form but not part of loosening of association.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true, except:

options.text: Autochthonous delusions are primary delusions
Delusions are systematized when delusions accumulate and become a complicated delusional system
Change of mood before a delusion is called Wahnstimmung
Capgras syndrome is a delusion in which a familiar person is replaced by an impostor
Delusional mood is a type of delusional memory

correct_answer.text: Delusional mood is a type of delusional memory

correct_answers.text: Delusional mood is a type of delusional memory

questions.explanation: Delusional mood is different from delusional memory. In delusional memory, past events are processed with new significance.

questions.question_text: Regarding depersonalization, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: The person feels unreal, detached from his /her own experience
It is a pleasant experience
The experience begins abruptly and lasts only a few minutes in healthy people
It is not diagnostic
It is experienced quite commonly as a transient phenomenon by healthy adults

correct_answer.text: It is a pleasant experience

correct_answers.text: It is a pleasant experience

questions.explanation: Depersonalization is reported to be a very unpleasant experience.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true regarding motor symptoms, except:

options.text: Tics are regular repeated movements involving a group of muscles
Mannerisms are repeated movements that appear to have some functional significance
Posturing is the adoption of unusual bodily postures continuously for a long time
Stereotypes are repeated movements that are regular and without obvious significance
Psychological pillow is a type of waxy flexibility

correct_answer.text: Tics are regular repeated movements involving a group of muscles

correct_answers.text: Tics are regular repeated movements involving a group of muscles

questions.explanation: Tics are irregular repeated movements.

questions.question_text: The following are all disorders of body image, except:

options.text: Coenestopathic state
Mitgehen
Phantom limb
Hemiasomatognosia
Reduplication phenomenon

correct_answer.text: Mitgehen

correct_answers.text: Mitgehen

questions.explanation: Mitgehen is abnormal body movement in which the patient's body movement can be initiated with the slightest pressure.

questions.question_text: Regarding memory, which of the following is false?

options.text: Semantic memory is concerned with factual information
Episodic memory is memory for experiences
Procedural memory is also called explicit memory
Prospective memory is also concerned with actions to be carried out in the near future
Working memory usually holds information for 15–20 seconds

correct_answer.text: Procedural memory is also called explicit memory

correct_answers.text: Procedural memory is also called explicit memory

questions.explanation: Procedural memory is implicit memory, in which patients cannot explain the steps for a procedure but can do it.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true, except:

options.text: Jamais vu is failure to recognize events that have been encountered before
De ´ja`vu is the conviction that an event has occurred when in fact it is novel
Retrograde amnesia is inability to recall events before onset of unconsciousness
In amnestic disorder, people can recall remote events but not events from a few minutes before
Anterograde amnesia is a disorder of recognition

correct_answer.text: Anterograde amnesia is a disorder of recognition

correct_answers.text: Anterograde amnesia is a disorder of recognition

questions.explanation: Anterograde amnesia is a disorder of memory.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true in types of impaired level of consciousness?

options.text: Oneiroid state is a dream-like state in sleep
T orpor is a state of impaired consciousness with no evidence of slow thinking
T wilight state is a prolonged oneiroid state
In stupor, reflexes are abnormal
The patient does not resist attempts to open a closed eye in stupor

correct_answer.text: T wilight state is a prolonged oneiroid state

correct_answers.text: T wilight state is a prolonged oneiroid state

questions.explanation: Oneiroid state occurs when the patient is not sleeping. T orpor occurs with slow thinking and narrowed range of perception. In stupor, reflexes are normal; usually the eyes are open and if they are closed the patient will resist any attempt to open them.

questions.question_text: In the Mini Mental State Examination:

options.text: Orientation to time, place and person are assessed
Constructional praxis is checked by clock drawing
Left-to-right orientation is assessed
Spelling 'world' backwards assesses concentration
Abstract reasoning is assessed by interpretation of proverbs

correct_answer.text: Spelling 'world' backwards assesses concentration

correct_answers.text: Spelling 'world' backwards assesses concentration

questions.explanation: Orientation to person is not assessed. Constructional praxis is checked by an interlocking pentagon. Abstract reasoning and left-to-right orientation are not assessed in the MMSE.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is false?

options.text: Language disorders point to left hemisphere in right-handed people
Dysarthria is difficulty in the production of speech by the speech organs
Dysphasia is partial failure of the language function of cortical origin
Receptive dysphasia suggests a posterior lesion
Language disorder with mainly visual dysphasia suggests an anterior lesion

correct_answer.text: Language disorder with mainly visual dysphasia suggests an anterior lesion

correct_answers.text: Language disorder with mainly visual dysphasia suggests an anterior lesion

questions.explanation: Language disorder with mainly visual dysphasia suggests a posterior lesion.

questions.question_text: Regarding scales, which of the following is false?

options.text: The Mini Mental State Examination has 30 items
The Hamilton Anxiety Scale has 21 items
The Montgomery–A ˚sberg Depression Rating Scale has 10 items
The Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale has 16 items
The Yale–Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale has 10 items

correct_answer.text: The Hamilton Anxiety Scale has 21 items

correct_answers.text: The Hamilton Anxiety Scale has 21 items

questions.explanation: In the Hamilton Anxiety Scale, 13 items are rated, using five-point scales.

questions.question_text: Regarding anxiety, which of the following is false?

options.text: Somatic anxiety is where the subject has increased tension and fearful apprehension
Anxiety symptoms are part of normal healthy experience
A moderate amount of anxiety can optimize performance
Anxiety symptoms may occur only episodically in panic attacks
Anxiety symptoms may not have an identifiable stimulus

correct_answer.text: Somatic anxiety is where the subject has increased tension and fearful apprehension

correct_answers.text: Somatic anxiety is where the subject has increased tension and fearful apprehension

questions.explanation: In psychic anxiety the subject has increased tension and fearful apprehension, while in somatic anxiety the patient has bodily sensations of palpitation and sweating.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a first-rank symptom?

options.text: Thought insertion
Thought echo
Thought withdrawal
Thought broadcasting
Thought block

correct_answer.text: Thought block

correct_answers.text: Thought block

questions.explanation: Thought block is not a Schneiderian first-rank symptom.

questions.question_text: In the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS), which of the following is false?

options.text: The total score is 15
A GCS score of 8 or less correlates with severe brain injury
A person able to speak only inappropriate words scores 3 in verbal response
A person able to flex only to pain scores 3 in motor response
The maximum score for verbal response is 6

correct_answer.text: The maximum score for verbal response is 6

correct_answers.text: The maximum score for verbal response is 6

questions.explanation: In the Glasgow Coma Scale, the best eye, verbal and motor response scores are 4, 5 and 6 respectively.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false?

options.text: The Wisconsin Card-Sorting T ask is used to assess frontal lobe functioning
The go/no-go test is used as part of the frontal assessment battery
Astereognosia is seen in non-dominant parietal lobe lesion
Gerstmann's syndrome is caused by a lesion of the dominant parietal lobe
The maximum score in the Mini Mental State Examination for assessing orientation is 10

correct_answer.text: Astereognosia is seen in non-dominant parietal lobe lesion

correct_answers.text: Astereognosia is seen in non-dominant parietal lobe lesion

questions.explanation: Astereognosis is failure to recognize the feel of objects with the eyes closed. It is seen in dominant parietal lobe lesions.

questions.question_text: All of the following physical signs could be suggestive of the corresponding physical illnesses, except:

options.text: Hamster face–bulimia nervosa
Lanugo hair–anorexia nervosa
Goose flesh–opiate withdrawal
Broad-based gait–cerebellar disease
Argyll Robertson pupil–Wilson's disease

correct_answer.text: Argyll Robertson pupil–Wilson's disease

correct_answers.text: Argyll Robertson pupil–Wilson's disease

questions.explanation: Argyll Robertson pupil is seen in neurosyphilis.

questions.question_text: All of the following can be described as features of schizophrenia, except:

options.text: Ambitendency
Asyndesis
Blunting of affect
Broca's dysphasia
Derailment

correct_answer.text: Broca's dysphasia

correct_answers.text: Broca's dysphasia

questions.explanation: Broca's dysphasia is not a feature of schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: Narcolepsy consists of all of the following, except:

options.text: Catalepsy
Excessive daytime sleepiness
Sleep paralysis
Sudden loss of muscle tone
Hypnagogic hallucinations

correct_answer.text: Catalepsy

correct_answers.text: Catalepsy

questions.explanation: This is a common question. It is cataplexy and not catalepsy that is seen in narcolepsy.

questions.question_text: First-rank symptoms include all of the following, except:

options.text: Somatic passivity
Passivity of volition
Paucity of speech
Passivity of impulse
Passivity of affect

correct_answer.text: Paucity of speech

correct_answers.text: Paucity of speech

questions.explanation: First-rank symptoms do not include paucity of speech.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is false?

options.text: Othello syndrome is delusional jealousy
Ekbom's syndrome is delusion of infestation
De Cle ´rambault's syndrome is delusion of love
Capgras syndrome is delusional misidentification
Fregoli's syndrome is delusion of reference

correct_answer.text: Fregoli's syndrome is delusion of reference

correct_answers.text: Fregoli's syndrome is delusion of reference

questions.explanation: Fregoli's syndrome is a type of delusional misidentification. The patient believes strangers have been replaced by familiar people.

questions.question_text: All of the following are synonyms, except:

options.text: Entgleiten–Derailment
Erotomania–Delusion of love
Ey syndrome–Othello syndrome
E´cho de la pense ´e–Thought echo
Gedankenlautwerden–Thought echo

correct_answer.text: Entgleiten–Derailment

correct_answers.text: Entgleiten–Derailment

questions.explanation: Entgleisen is a synonym for derailment. Entgleiten is a synonym for thought blocking.

questions.question_text: All of the following are features of Wernicke's encephalopathy, except:

options.text: Ophthalmoplegia
Nystagmus
Ataxia
Acute confusional state
It is caused mainly by vitamin B12 deficiency

correct_answer.text: It is caused mainly by vitamin B12 deficiency

correct_answers.text: It is caused mainly by vitamin B12 deficiency

questions.explanation: Wernicke's encephalopathy is caused by vitamin B1 deficiency and not B12. The other four are the classical tetrad in Wernicke's.

questions.question_text: Regarding normal-pressure hydrocephalus, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: Dementia is irreversible
Gait ataxia is present
Urinary incontinence usually appears later
Dilation of cerebral ventricles is present
24-hour intracranial pressure monitoring shows a typical 'beta' pattern

correct_answer.text: Dementia is irreversible

correct_answers.text: Dementia is irreversible

questions.explanation: Dementia is potentially reversible if treated promptly.

questions.question_text: In Parkinson's disease, all of the following are seen, except:

options.text: Cog-wheel rigidity
Resting tremor
Bradykinesia
Negative glabellar tap
Autonomic instability

correct_answer.text: Negative glabellar tap

correct_answers.text: Negative glabellar tap

questions.explanation: In Parkinson's disease there is usually positive glabellar tap.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not part of the widely propounded principles of moral philosophy and ethics proposed by Beauchamp and Childress (1994)?

options.text: Autonomy
Beneficence
Non-maleficence
Logical analysis
Justice

correct_answer.text: Logical analysis

correct_answers.text: Logical analysis

questions.explanation: The other four form the principles of moral philosophy and ethics.

questions.question_text: Regarding principles of confidentiality, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: Wherever possible, identifiable data should be used
Disclosure should be done only after consent
Children over a stated age (usually 16) should enjoy the same rights as adults
Disclosure of information should be kept to a minimum
Effective measures should be taken to protect personal information

correct_answer.text: Wherever possible, identifiable data should be used

correct_answers.text: Wherever possible, identifiable data should be used

questions.explanation: Non-identifiable data should be used.

questions.question_text: Medical treatment may be given in all of the following situations, except:

options.text: When the patient has offered written consent
In an emergency
When it is considered in the best interest of an unconscious patient
When it is for a patient with capacity who has refused consent
When the patient has given implied consent

correct_answer.text: When it is for a patient with capacity who has refused consent

correct_answers.text: When it is for a patient with capacity who has refused consent

questions.explanation: Consent is needed in a patient with capacity.

questions.question_text: Under the Mental Capacity Act 2007, a patient is stated to have capacity if he/she is able to do all of the following, except:

options.text: Comprehend the information
Believe the information
Retain the information
Make an informed choice
Communicate his /her decision

correct_answer.text: Believe the information

correct_answers.text: Believe the information

questions.explanation: In the latest Act, the 'believe' part has been omitted.

questions.question_text: Legal criteria for assessing testamentary capacity include all of the following, except:

options.text: Whether a testator understands what a will is and what its consequences are
Whether he /she knows the nature and extent of the property
Whether he /she knows the names of close relatives and can assess their claims to the property
Whether he /she has suffered any mental illness in the past
Whether he /she is free from an abnormal state of mind that might distort feelings or judgements relevant to making the will

correct_answer.text: Whether he /she has suffered any mental illness in the past

correct_answers.text: Whether he /she has suffered any mental illness in the past

questions.explanation: T estamentary capacity does not deal with past history.

questions.question_text: Regarding driving after an illness, the Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency regulations include all of the following, except:

options.text: One year off driving after a solitary fit
4 weeks off driving after the event if the person has loss of conscious-ness likely to be unexplained syncope and low risk of recurrence
Must not drive for at least one month after a cerebrovascular disease
Must not drive after a diagnosis of dementia
3 months off driving after the person has been well and stable after an acute psychotic disorder, compliant with treatment and receives a favourable specialist report

correct_answer.text: Must not drive after a diagnosis of dementia

correct_answers.text: Must not drive after a diagnosis of dementia

questions.explanation: People with mild dementia may drive after notifying the DVLA if they have been found fit to drive, though they may have to undergo a special extended driving test.

questions.question_text: According to the Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency, a person suffering from schizophrenia or other chronic psychosis can restart driving after an acute episode if he/she satisfies all of the following conditions, except:

options.text: Stable behaviour for at least 3 months
Adequately compliant with treatment
Free from adverse effects of medication that would impair driving
Subject to a favourable specialist report
Should have full insight

correct_answer.text: Should have full insight

correct_answers.text: Should have full insight

questions.explanation: The DVLA checks fitness to drive.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is false regarding General Medical Council guidelines for informing the Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency?

options.text: The DVLA is legally responsible for deciding if a patient is medically unfit to drive
The doctor should request the patient to inform the DVLA if the patient has a condition which impairs the ability to drive
The doctor has to inform the DVLA without the patient's knowledge of any condition which could impair the ability to drive
If the patient does not accept the diagnosis or effect of the condition on ability to drive, the doctor should suggest a second opinion
If the patient continues to drive when not fit to do so, the doctor should make every reasonable effort to persuade the patient to stop

correct_answer.text: The doctor has to inform the DVLA without the patient's knowledge of any condition which could impair the ability to drive

correct_answers.text: The doctor has to inform the DVLA without the patient's knowledge of any condition which could impair the ability to drive

questions.explanation: The patient should be notified or informed before the doctor informs the DVLA if necessary.

questions.question_text: Confidentiality may be broken in all the following situations, except:

options.text: T o assist in the prevention or detection of a crime
If a close friend wants to know the diagnosis against the patient's wishes
If the general public are at serious risk
If the patient continues to drive when unfit to do so and against medical advice
For notification of a known or suspected communicable disease

correct_answer.text: If a close friend wants to know the diagnosis against the patient's wishes

correct_answers.text: If a close friend wants to know the diagnosis against the patient's wishes

questions.explanation: Patient consent is needed if no risk issues are identified.

questions.question_text: In relation to the Mental Health Act 1983, which of the following is incorrect?

options.text: Section 5(4) is holding power for a maximum of 72 hours
Section 2 provides authority for a patient to be detained in hospital for assessment for a maximum of 28 days
Section 136 is for police to take a person in a public place who is considered to be mentally disordered to a 'place of safety'
Section 3 is a treatment order initially for a maximum period of 6 months
Section 2 cannot be renewed or extended after 28 days

correct_answer.text: Section 5(4) is holding power for a maximum of 72 hours

correct_answers.text: Section 5(4) is holding power for a maximum of 72 hours

questions.explanation: Section 5(4) is about nurses holding power for 6 hours.
